tips.comment: A tentative pick goes on Paul Nicholls' Keel Strand. It comes into this following wind surgery plus the addition of a first-time tongue tie.

Won at Huntingdon on hurdles debut for trainer Jamie Snowden in early May and looked a very good prospect and went into my tracker. A 2 time winner on the flat for David O'Meara at a class 5 level and has the best form on offer here by far in a race that could easily fall apart. Strong fancy but price does reflect his chance.

Gary and Josh Moore have this seven-year-old racing under their banner for the first time since leaving the point-to-point world, trained by Elizabeth Feakes. Highway Hero stayed on strongly at Godstone over twenty furlongs and got up by a short head to win. Twenty-one and a half furlongs here can play to his stamina strengths and take this novice race, which does not look the strongest on paper. Highway Hero is by Millenary, and his sire is Rainbow Quest, and dam sire is Dancing Brave. I should say for both was, as both of those talented horses are no longer with us. If this lad has their attitude, which he may have with him winning his point-to-point with a powerful finish, he could be showing his strengths of stamina and determination here.

OVAL STREET (25/1) has been inconsistent over hurdles but has been placed three times, including over this course and distance. Last time out, he finished 4th in a decent race, and that's good form back in this race.
The four in front of him in the market have significant questions to answer. Favourite, Knights Affair, won his debut hurdle race last time, but he did not beat anything special and now carries a 6lb penalty for that. Keel Stand is surely short-priced due to being a Nichol-trained horse, having been well-beaten on both hurdle starts to date. Chief Black Robe has some good chase form but atrocious hurdle form, so I really don't know why he's trying again here. Highway Hero pulled up on his only hurdle start last time.
OVAL STREET is not perfect by any means, but he has a good chance in this field.

Illogical Logic returns to Newton Abbot a week after his unfortunate jumping lapse at the second last fence when looking to have the race won. That was a two mile five furlong chase and he moves up in distance here but there is no reason to doubt his stamina and he is normally a safe jumper.

Has some solid form here in the past, twice placed over 2m5f here when doing the best of his work late. Fell at the last over this trip here in August when challenging for third from a 4lb higher mark. Capable of hitting the frame once again.

Took his first chase win in his penultimate outing (fifth chase run) with a win in a Class 5, 3m handicap chase (Gd) so I think we can maybe give him the benefit of the doubt for his latest effort (25 days ago and only 2 weeks after his win) when he trailed in 50L behind the winner (today’s runner Grand Sabre) after putting in a poor round of jumping.
Running today off a mark 4lbs higher than his recent win, he has shown he can jump and has the ability to win races, so, with B. Doyle back in the saddle today (rode him when winning penultimate race), 5.50 looks a fair price to take for him to bounce back with a decent effort

A much improved performance at Warwick last time, 1/5 jumping better than his previous run over fences, being set off at 20/1. Shows the improvement made. That sort of form will put him in the mix this afternoon. Each-way bet advised.

The favorite here would have won by a long way last time and has probably improved for cheekpieces, but his overall profile would say he is one to take on at a short price. Tellairsue was shorter in the market than the favorite for the race here last time on his chase debut. He was disappointing there, but judging by the SP, better was expected. With that experience, he could improve and could look a big price.
A progressive, improving horse that has been raised 7lb in the weights but could still progress more and complete a 3-timer in a weak-looking race.

He's down to a mark of 103, 9 lbs below the mark he ran off in this very race last season. He won this race convincingly last term, running on strongly to win going away at the line. A solid performance given he was a couple of lengths down back in 3rd place jumping the hurdle. He ran on nicely to win easily. He's a real course specialist here, boasting 6 wins and 4 places from 13 runs at this particular track. Rarely runs a bad race around here, which is a huge plus at this tricky venue. I like the booking of Harry Cobden. That looks to be a signal of intent. Clearly, the yard is hopeful of him running another big race at his favourite venue.

The Tom Lacey yard is flying at the moment, and Luttrell Lad ran well last time out in a decent class 2 handicap. He drops in class here, and most of his rivals move into a class 3 after running in a lower grade last time out. With the yard going so well, I think he has a class edge on this field and looks a value price.
A winner of four in his last five starts which include back to back wins since returning after wind surgery. 4lb rise fair and he was a winner at this course last time out over a furlong shorter.

The Warren Greatrex trained Alba Crus wasn't disgraced when finishing 2 3/4l behind Suspected when fifth of 10 on his racecourse debut at Uttoxeter over 2m (good) 10 days ago. He should have come on plenty for that run and could prove hard to beat.
The stable does not have a great record in these types of races, but it looks significant that the stable has booked Harry Cobhen, so it might have shown something at home.
Making a debut here, but there's only one horse in this race with a previous run. So, looking at pedigree is important. It is a half-sibling to multiple winning horses, so it could go well.
Going for a Dutch. Just like this one up in trip, been given some odd rides over shorter and early money suggests a big run is expected.
Feel like Chabadatika seems to be the one to be with here, given the liking for better ground and the ability to beat peers here, you would think.

Portobello Girl has drifted out in the market a tiny bit this morning to a just backable e/w shot. She did well to win last time out at Stratford, switching and then going up the inside rail and finishing strongly. Also she was a decent 2nd at Uttoxeter. So she obviously had the stamina for this distance. She should be close. 3 places.

Inchagoill Lady hit top form on first try at 3m on good to firm ground in April and was then dropped markedly in trip last month for a run here. After being held up she lacked the pace to get into the finish. Stepped back up to 3m again and she has an opportunity to pick up the winning thread in this.
All Under Control was just denied by a late challenge by Portobello Girl last time at Stratford and she could get her revenge on three pounds better terms at Newton Abbot.

ELFRIDE won a 3 mile hurdle at Uttoxeter in May 2023 but has done little since. She goes off the same mark for the first time since here and could benefit from the application of first time blinkers. She has had 6 weeks off and could benefit from that break and she will benefit from the claim of Harry Atkins who has a 32% record for having his rides finish in the first 3.
Culligran made an encouraging start to chasing when a good second at Ffos Las two weeks ago and the step up in distance will suit her.
Fever Dream could be a big player here for Christian Williams. He has the form in the book to take this race, and I fancy him to do so.

Yet to shine over fences and made a bad mistake latest in a chase at Clonmel. Did still finish fourth, and that was better form than it looks. Could go well here and has scope as a chaser. Has a good level of form over hurdles, winning twice last season.
Just might bounce back from a very poor run last time out at Plumpton, but did go off fancied that day. It's too early to write off yet. Might be seen better now back chasing.

Seraphic came close to losing his maiden tag over hurdles in March when Greatness Awaits fought back on the run-in to beat him by a neck. He has since won on the flat at Brighton over ten furlongs and could get his first hurdles win off a mark of 91.
Just a really interesting handicap debutant after some low-key runs in his qualifying runs. Some money for it this morning and it wouldn't be the first Honeyball horse to improve in this discipline.

John Betjeman is a seasoned campaigner at this level and knows Newton Abbot well, having won over course and distance before. His comeback run in April was below par, but he's entitled to come on for it. Trainer Mark Gillard has a knack for bringing them on after a run, and regular rider Joe Anderson is back on board. He's running off a workable mark of 95 and has the experience and tactical speed to get involved in a race like this. If he finds anything like his best form, he’s a real each-way player.

Hill Station had his first run for 107 days last time and his first over hurdles since September 2023. Given a wide run and an educating ride, he went well for a long way until tiring and being eased. Jumped most flights fluently and well. Dropped 5lb for that and the rider's claim takes another 5lb off. Looked a winner at this track in 2022 when falling at the second last 2m1f good after making most. He could try to make all today and looks capable of hanging on.

WHISPERING ROYAL is back racing over his likely still optimum distance today and he could be about to come back to hand. No doubt a well treated racer who is not highly-tried in the handicap hurdles sphere and he could get competitive at rewarding odds.

Athough they would look a no hoper here based on their non handicap hurdles to date, they were all @ class 4 level and Lto one was not without merit. Is a nicely bred horse having come out of the J. Bolger yard in Ireland, makes handicap debut here in a class 5 off lowly mark of 81, good jockey who does well for this stable retains ride and shrewd trainer has done well here last 5 seasons @ one of his local tracks, making current 33/1 decent Ew value in the race.

The model has suggested a large upset could be caused by Miss Marette and is the value bet for this race. Miss Marette lines up here with the second highest RPR compared to the rest of this 11-horse field but has an official ranking materially lower. This results in Miss Marette carrying significantly less weight around this 2m handicap hurdle. Tries blinkers for the first time, which is interesting at 9 years old. Previous distance winner and last ran 14 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern.
This colt has placed on both previous runs over similar ground, and he remains unexposed with scope to improve, especially now stepping up in trip, which could unlock further progression.
Making debut against more experienced horses here, but comes from a really good pedigree, so merits a punt at a decent price.

Padesha, owned by Amo Racing, has David Egan here in the saddle for two rides and has not gone to The Curragh or Ripon where the owners have runners. David Egan being here sees him riding earlier for connections on a favorite and this gelding, who is by Wootton Bassett, may show potential here with this being his second run after being gelded and now his fifth race of his career. We might see him being aggressive at the finish for a result.
Boyfriend nearly made all when a close second in a C2 on the return last month when headed towards the finish. I would expect more now, second up and dropping back to C4.
Thyer is the choice in this race on balance. Had some disappointing races over in Meydan, but the first race back on these shores has thrown up a few placed horses. Has a good chance here.

Metallo steps into this Class 4 handicap off a mark of 85, which is fair based on his earlier all-weather form. He was a bit keen and faded late at Newmarket last time, but the switch to a visor might help him settle. Drawn in stall 1 with Rossa Ryan up, he’s got the tools to bounce back if he gets a smoother trip.

Both wins have been over 7f, but one on good/soft, the other at tougher Leicester. So, distance-wise, I think Madame De Sevigne can get a mile and a win. Has a couple of good place efforts at Newmarket and has to be in the pack here.
High Approval, a 2-year-old bay colt, is making his debut here for H Al Jenani. A very expensive purchase who is expected to make his presence felt here.

Side Deal was a bit raw at York when finishing 2nd despite a slow start, then hanging left 2f out and still gaining the lead 1f out, only to weaken late on and just hold on for 2nd. That was a decent class 2 6f novice race, and he could win this provided High Approval does not match his stablemate Postmodern, who slaughtered the field at Yarmouth, which included both Silent Applause and Front Line Fury.

Makes racecourse debut today for trainer Karl Burke, who does well with his 2-year-olds and has a 17% strike rate at Nottingham. An expensive purchase and well-bred, who probably could race over further in time. Any support in the market would be significant.

I was all ready to tip Front Line Fury and I've bottled it. SA cost a fortune at the Craven Breeze Up and must surely have more to offer second time up. The difference in price between the two makes no sense based on that last run, so they must be expecting better this time out. There are two shorties heading the market, which is why I've changed to this one and it will serve me right if I miss out. Moscow Power is another at a price that could do better than the odds are showing.

Zelaina was picked up at a Breeze Up sale for £650k and is thought highly of amongst Karl Burke's string. She is put up against newcomers from several top stables but should take advantage of her draw near the stands side at Nottingham.
Novelette, a 2-year-old bay filly. Another expensive breeze-up sale purchase with S & E Crisford. Their 2-year-olds are running well this season. Might be worth an each-way bet.

Rossa Ryan is in the plate once more with the Godolphin blue here for Charlie Appleby with this Lope De Vega filly having debut run, could be full of promise with conditions bringing the best out of her.
Monsieur Patat may cope with a four-pound penalty for his win at Windsor after a break from running on the all-weather. The eight-year-old was held up and had to wait for a gap but won convincingly.

Once rated 81 on the flat and now down to 61. Raced over course and distance in August 2024 off a mark of 72 and beaten three quarters of a length, 4th of 11. Worth a look off this mark and will welcome the drop in trip after racing over 7 furlongs at Chelmsford last time out.
Failed in his hat-trick bid when 7th of 8 in an apprentice handicap at Salisbury but lost all chance after stumbling from the stalls. Hector Crouch is on board today and should run better.

This mediocre-looking class six handicap could go to Roy Bowring's Toptime, who last won at Southwell in December over the minimum trip off just a two lb lower mark than the one of 61 he carries here. Today, he moves back up to six furlongs, a distance he is equally comfortable with, and has Lewis Edmunds, who gets on well with him, onboard again.
Expect that the horse needed the run first time out. As this horse remains relatively unexposed, the booking of Hollie Doyle points to a better performance here than the odds suggest.

Sounds Of Spring goes well with cut in the ground and returns from a break here. He’s a four-time winner, mostly on softer going, so quicker ground might not be ideal. If there’s any ease underfoot and he’s fit, he could run better than the odds suggest.
Soul Dance has been a bit down the pack for all three runs so far. But what catches my eye is the booking of Oisin Murphy for this handicap debut, which could be enough to put her in with a chance.

Only managed 6th over this course and distance a few starts back but was hampered for a lot of the race and would have gone close with a clear run. Got a deserved win last time when winning with a bit to spare. Sure to go close. Forecast 11/4.

A nice run from the 3yo filly four weeks ago on her handicap debut on the AW. She finished 3rd and was beaten just a length after coming off a 6-month break. Unexposed after just four starts, the switch to turf could bring about more improvement. Same mark for this handicap, facing lower-rated rivals, and she has a strong jockey booking.

Skyelight did not match her all-weather form in her latest run on turf at Windsor. She started her two-year-old career with a promising run at Nottingham, which meant she was then outclassed in her next race behind the still unbeaten Oaks favourite, Desert Flower. She is, however, capable of competing in a Class 5 handicap, dropped to a mark of 58.

Useful filly at this level. She won on the all-weather in December at Southwell and was 4/13 last time out 14 days ago at Kempton, which was a good step forward. Yet to show on turf, but maybe today she can make that improvement. With 3 places on offer and the fact that Hector Crouch rides her regularly gives her good each-way appeal.

This one's only start on turf was her first race in a maiden where she outran her odds. After a few races on the A/W, she is sent back on the turf again on good/firm ground. On a decent handicap mark for an in-form stable, she looks a bet at the price.

Shielas Well did great in September with two wins before the break. She has returned in April to three improving runs, so it should be fit and is now back on that last winning mark. Worth an EW chance.

Saint Bibiana is not penalized for winning a weak four-horse conditional jockeys' handicap hurdle last week. If fully recovered, he could follow up under Olive Nicholls in this amateur jockeys' handicap hurdle.

The model I run suggests Hostile Hotelier can win this one. Hostile Hotelier lines up here with the second highest RPR of this small 5-runner field and has the highest official ranking. This, however, still looks like Hostile Hotelier is racing off a competitive mark with the other market leaders all in and around the same weight. Comes here in decent form with figures of 2162-3, with the most recent outing a decent 3rd at Hexham over 3m. The extra 2f might be helpful here as stayed on well for a good second at Sedgefield in April when chasing. Back over hurdles here where the last win came in March. Edward Vaughan on board relieves further 5 lb off his back, so could go close here today. model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

An outside chance here, previously with Shark Hanlon but has moved to a new yard, so this may spark improvements. Jullou De Grissay did show promise when finishing a close fourth in a strong maiden at Gowran last September, keeping something in reserve late on. Though he didn't quite match that form next time and has been off the track since, the recent runs in points suggest he's been sharpening up. Could be a solid each-way chance if returning to that earlier level here.
Ice In The Veins overcame trouble in running to win a bumper at Worcester last month and looks good for this maiden hurdle provided he has been well schooled by the Skeltons.

Race 2 at Warwick today is a Maiden (Class 4) Hurdle race for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,219 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Belcamo from the Alex Hales yard, and will be ridden by Harry Bannister. This son of Belardo is a consistent enough performer, and one can put a line through his latest when finishing a distance behind the winner. He was subsequently given a deserved rest, and looking at the rest of the field in this race, he should be a major player on form alone.

Shadows In The Sky won his third handicap chase at Uttoxeter in May but could not follow up at Huntingdon three days later when 2nd. All of those races were at two and a half miles, and he has yet to win a hurdle or chase at this distance. However, he was a winning pointer at three miles in November 2022 and should be able to stay.

Excuses the last twice. Needed the reappearance run last time, running over hurdles and soft ground on the last run of the season last year. Only a couple of pounds higher than when failing by a neck to get up 3 runs back.

Off the Mark over fences after 4 attempts at Chepstow. However, was a disappointing favourite at Sedgefield, but 10 fences were omitted. With Sean Bowen booked for this ride, it should be a great each-way shout.
There's a bit of value to be had with Mrs Tabitha. Timeform has her down as unreliable, but she's been running well over fences, and her stats compare favorably with market rivals. Chance.

Okavango Delta has to overcome another rise in his mark following his win at Worcester in May, where he was helped by the fall of Abingworth two out when challenging. But his jumping may see him through against Fancy Stuff, who jumped badly here previously.

The model I run suggests Fancy Stuff can win this one. Fancy Stuff lines up here with the second highest RPR of the small 4-runner field. Has shown decent form recently with a good second at Stratford over a similar distance and looks to get over the line first here. Last ran 17 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. Sean Bowen, champion jockey, picks up the reins and can make the difference in what looks like a tight tactical race. Fancy Stuff carries a stone less than the current market leader on this 2m 4f trip. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The Nicky Henderson-trained Therapist won by 12 lengths at Stratford last time out, ridden by Freddie Gordon, who stays on board to use his claim as she has a lot of weight. This looks slightly more competitive, but the way she won last time out suggests she will handle the 5 lbs penalty. Despite a slight drift in the market at the time of writing, I think she has every chance of landing the hat-trick.
Blazeon Five looks to have a good opportunity here at Warwick tonight. Appears to have a very lenient handicap mark starting out for Alan King.

The model I run suggests Soleil d'Arizona can win this race. Soleil d'Arizona lines up here with the second highest RPR of this smaller 5 horse race but looks better treated off this lower official ranking than some of the other runners. The current market favourite is the top weight and gives away over a stone to Soleil d'Arizona in weight difference. Comes here in decent form and a good second at this course in May. Same class race here and looks to go one better. The first came at Haydock but in a higher class race. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Faced a tough task, finishing third, 5.5 lengths behind in a 2m1f handicap hurdle at Bangor on Dee last time. Likely to improve from the outing; will be Therapist.
Princess T is not without an outside chance in this small race. Won in October at Wincanton and today refitted with cheekpieces.
Byzantium has a promising 5lb claimer riding here and looks a huge price at 11/2. There for the each way thieves to get stuck into tonight.

Very lightly raced 6yo and we haven't see the best of her yet and I'm expecting an improved run for recent spin after break since November. Dam is the very smart Snow Leopardess who won at around this trip as a 4yo before going on to win at Grade 3 and Listed level including a Becher Chase. Good ground is fine and can prove profitable to follow this year. Hopefully can shed maiden tag soon and looks well handicapped to me as must be better to come.

The model I run suggests Hardy Buck as the outside value bet here. Hardy Buck lines up with a similar RPR to the rest of the field but has an official ranking considerably lower. Subsequently, it goes out carrying much less weight than the market leaders. A stone less over 2m 3f can be telling. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Orionis has only had three runs and has improved with each outing, with the latest being second in a C2. Tom remains in the saddle for this drop to C5, and I would expect more today.

Three turf runs for the 5yo this year, shaping a bit better last time out, not landing a blow but staying on at the finish. He started last year slowly before finding his form and running some nice races last summer off a 10lb higher mark. He could be ready to strike.
Although Mr. Midgley runs the top weight and paper favorite, his last year's winner, Herakles, may be the one to be on now back on a good mark.

Jojo Rabbit is one I have to go for as he is an old favorite of mine that often surprises with a win. While not winning since July last year off a 70, he is on a falling mark, and I think today's 62 could put him back in the money each way, having had three improving runs since the break in April.

Dark Kestrel has been dropped to his lowest ever mark of 65 but he has had wind surgery since his latest run and should be competitive provided he does not have a poor start which he has been prone to.

Caesars Pearl is down another 3 pounds today, so could be within an each-way shot. He has struggled to recapture winning form recently and looks a bit out of sorts on the all-weather, but I do not discount a bounce back here, dropping so much in the weights after watching his last runs.

Precious Spartan appeared to benefit from the recent move to local trainer Patrick Neville and ran away with a similar course and distance handicap last week and could cope with the six pound penalty as the handicapper is due to put him up eight pounds. Jason Hart takes over the ride.

Epicurian Lad is still searching for his first win, but there are signs he might be getting closer. He’s been running respectably in Class 5 handicaps, including a fourth at Ripon in April and a sixth at Nottingham last time out. Now dropped into Class 6 company and fitted with a first-time visor, he could find the improvement needed.

Flamborough Head ran a good second at this track two runs back considering how keen he was in the early stages. I hope David Allan can settle him better this time, and, if he can, he could be a force to be reckoned with at the business end of the race.

Timeless Spirit is one interesting contender here and for very good reason was last seen at Nottingham 36 days ago where finishing 5th/12 outrunning her huge odds of 40/1 in the process and was unlucky not to have finished much closer as she was denied a clear run at a very crucial stage of that race when making good headway from the rear of the field and finished with plenty left in the tank that was also her seasonal reappearance run and handicap debut after a 122 day break and shaped with plenty of promise under the circumstances entitled to strip much fitter that run under her belt worth noting that was the second time this individual has outran huge odds and is most certainly one to keep a close eye on currently operating on a mark of 64 this daughter of Time Test & Perfect Spirit ( Dam's sire Invincible Spirit ) looks more than capable of getting off the mark now arriving here in a much fitter state jockey Ryhs Elliot takes off a valuable 5lb which only enhances his good looking claims here

Trained by Charlie Johnston, this three-year-old gelding got off the mark in good style at Wolverhampton in March, landing a Class 6 handicap over 7 furlongs. He followed that up with a fair effort back at the same track later that month, finishing sixth in a Class 5, beaten just over four lengths.
The switch to turf now could really suit. He’s bred to handle it and the stiff finish at Ripon might help bring his stamina into play over this mile trip. This drop back into Class 6 company also gives him a chance to get competitive again, and with that win under his belt and a bit of improvement still to come, he’s definitely one to keep on side for place money at the very least.

Hoping the dropped mark will help her get back to the kind of form that saw her finish a useful 2 of 5 at Musselburgh back in April of this year, which was off a higher mark. She can perform strongly if improvements are made.
Caledonian Dream is an entire, and the trainer has done a fantastic job to get him down to this low mark. Ran well last time after a decent break and has every chance of making hay here.

This horse makes his handicap debut here after 3 quiet runs to get a handicap mark of 61. That's very much the stables modus operandi though, and there's every chance that we will see a big improvement now that the horse is upped in trip and with a very useful 3lb claiming Apprentice booked who is an incredible 7 from 18 for the stable. Clearly the trainer doesn't book him lightly and in addition to that Ripon is the course where the jockey has his most success. The horse is well bred too for a low level handicapper and I think a speculative punt could be the order of the day here.
Mart looks the standout here after recovering from a pretty awful position in an apprentice race to win and comes here without the penalty too. Good chance here.
Sacred Falls has run well this season. At Catterick last time, it was very unlucky at Carlisle when badly hampered. It is certainly capable of better than bare form.

Hectic hasn't been with this yard long but ran a cracker last time out in first-time cheekpieces. He was 4th of 20 in a very competitive race at York. He drops in class here and is on his last winning mark. A repeat of that should see him go close.
Has to be considered now, dropping back in company here. Won Class Four back in April and should go well here. Sacred Falls looks the danger.

Ripon isn't far away from me, and if the weather the past couple of days has been anything to go by, I doubt the going is still good by the time we get to 19:52. Therefore, from a good draw and at a decent price, I'm also tipping Emperor Caradoc here to place. Loves the softer ground conditions.
Second last two times, Beaton favorite forcing the pace. Jockey and trainer in good form. Will be there at the finish. Excellent each way chance at 8/1.

One More Dream went off the favorite last time and ran like it until the end when it could not get a split and was taken back, only to burst through. Unlucky. Alex Jary takes over with his claim and looks overpriced

This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, and they have got the same jockey on board as they are reapplying the cheekpieces on this one. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.
Harry's Halo has been well-backed this morning and is a good each-way bet. Won twice in the autumn and tried this time without headgear.
A strong pace here could tee it up nicely for this closer, who has looked in solid form recently. He has not benefited from a race run to suit, and this could be a good opportunity.

EW 4 Places. C&D Winner. 5lb rise for latest win, but rider's claim negates that. Alex Jary 20% SR at Ripon (1-5), but 14.18% for yard, +£8.50 to £1 Stake. Better draw in Stall 1. Seb Spencer with LTO winners - 18.8% SR, 62.5% Placed - +£6.22 to £1 EW Stake - 1.2 A/E. Territories 20.8% Sire Stat at Ripon - +£7.37 LSP. Stall 1 over 1m - 17.7% SR, 1.05 A/E. Won here last time, kicking clear with 3f to run, 11.61s 6th furlong (Ranked 1), 2nd and 4th both placed next start.

The 4yo lost his way for his previous yard last year in his three runs last spring. Better form on the AW after joining this yard last autumn. He ran well on turf as a 2yo, comes here fresh after a six week break and the return to grass could be a big plus. He has been rated 17lb higher as a 2yo.
Trainer won this race last year and hoping to do the double today. Will run well on this ground and likes the 1m distance. Good trainer and jockey combo.

Catton Lady was well held on her seasonal debut last time out. She could have needed that, and I think towards the back end of last season there were a few excuses with her. She was 3rd, beaten a length off 70 at Beverley last season, then ran over wrong trips or on soft ground. 1m should suit, and back on better ground after that pipe opener, she could be well in off 65.

Alfie Boy is back at Ripon after a couple of solid wins earlier this season. He made all to score at Beverley and Ayr, showing he can dictate from the front. Last time at Beverley, he pulled too hard and faded, but that’s not unusual for his running style. He’s only 3lb higher than his last win and has a decent draw in stall 5. If he settles better, he could bounce back in a race that suits front-runners.

Code Purple ran a solid second at Musselburgh over 8f, showing he can handle pressure despite making his move a bit too soon. At 16/1, he’s a strong each-way chance who should be in the mix again with a sharper ride from Paddy Mulrennan.

CARNIVAL ZAIN misfired last time out but still looks well handicapped based on the run in the big field at Thirsk the run before that. Looks to be well drawn and has potential if back in that mood. Well below the weights of last season's peak and could pick up the consistency and land a race of this calibre before too long.

Making strides from earlier efforts to achieve success in the 9 runner handicap at Southwell 34 days ago, following a noteworthy race. He holds value, considering his consistent form from last season. An each-way bet at 18/1 looks promising for a profitable return.

The Richard Fahey strike rate hasn't been at quite the level we're used to lately, but there are some clear signs that he's turning the corner. This horse could surprise on his debut run for the new stable. The horse's second in a Doncaster maiden is the piece of form which catches the eye here for this horse's chances. He was staying on into second over a furlong less, and the first and fourth have franked that form since. The horse's chances would improve further if the ground rode on the easy side of good. On the evidence of that maiden, it's clear that he's well handicapped if back to anything like that level of form after a spell of racing on the AW.
Strongly supported, finished a half-length second in a Pontefract maiden last time, showing significant improvement from a lackluster debut. Major claims.
A huge amount of cash must've been put down on this one from the Raphael Freire yard as the price has already plummeted from an opening show of 14/1, I'm following the money too.
A little disappointing on debut, but I would expect a big improvement here. Nothing jumps off the page against him, and he should go close.

Although not having had many runners at this course, this stable's strike rate does stand out with a nice profit. It does well with their 2-year-old runners, so this one looks like good each-way value in its debut race.

Showed good ability in debut run in the U.K. when 2 of 10 at Thirsk last month but then struggled LTO at Doncaster also last month. I think the sire, Ubettabelieveit (IRE), who has a strong strike rate, might be the difference, and going down in class should help.
Making debut but going for a speculative punt based on pedigree, as no fewer than four half-brothers have already proven victorious. So, could be one to watch.

Amadeus Mozart is taken to score in this high-quality maiden contest at seven furlongs at the Curragh. Aidan O'Brien (SR 33%) trains three of the ten runners. All three look useful. Amadeus Mozart is the eldest of the three, a February foal. Ballydoyle bred, by Wootton Bassett out of a Galileo mare. Market confidence. Choice of Ryan Moore. The name of the horse suggests they hope for big things. Henri Matisse and Camille Pissarro are some painterly Group 1 winners this year following Auguste Rodin winning a recent Derby. I suspect Amadeus Mozart has a bit of class.

Solid debut behind a good Coolmore winner in a similar level maiden over 6f here @ the Curragh. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, is related to winners, step up to this 7f a plus, good jockey retains ride and very good trainer best here with his 2yo's last 5 seasons, making current 7/1 very good Ew value against the hot favourite in the race.

With Ryan Moore selecting Amadeus Mozart the price about Dorset is a tempting one. He is at least as well related as his more fancied stablemate though 3 months younger so perhaps not as forward in himself but on paper at least he is likely to be more suited by this trip than Amadeus Mozart whose dam was bred to go much further than 7f.
Far too big a price for Ipanema Beach, who has shown ability on first two starts. Hoping this horse is able to use their experience to go close here.

Nod Of Approval is a 2yo colt trained by Mrs. John Harrington. He makes his debut and has a lovely pedigree, being related to three winners and out of an unraced dam who is a sister related to 8 individual winners who amassed 40 wins. Four of them posted career-high RPRs of 101, 108, 115, and 115. Nod Of Approval may well need the run, but Mrs. John Harrington knows how to ready a 2yo, landing 194 winners with her 2yos and 130 under today's jockey, Shane Foley. Interesting at 20-1.

Trying to work out how certain trainers plot and calculate their way around races, marks etc, etc, is all part of the game, for them and us. I don't know much about this trainer, but i have been keeping a closer eye out for any signs or trends this season and there are a few things i'm looking into. One is this 7lb claimer, who won on Lovely at 40-1 a few days ago. (did also ride time before & only 9/12 by 5l) Also a 2nd place 2 days before that win at 25-1, then mid May another 2nd at 22-1 and in April a paid place 4th/13 at 100-1. It won't and hasn't always been the case and this is a 2yo, but was sent out on first race over 5f and faded last furlong (not sure he's a sprinter) and is up in trip to 7f today with first time blinkers, so could be worth a small ew at 125-1.

Evening Blues has the experience of two good runs against decent opposition including Albert Einstein last time where the front two pulled well clear and despite being a late foal he has developed well and should be capable of holding off some potentially good newcomers.
Flushing Meadows has a top speed pedigree and his yard really believe in him. R L Moore and AP O'Brien do really well at the Curragh and I have got to like the price.
Killourney Reigns is nicely priced here and could run a decent race. Met trouble in running last time out and still finished not too far back. Can step up on that in a hot-looking handicap.

Evening Blues has some experience which will be useful but I'd make Lewis Carroll just about the best bred of these and despite Ryan Moore looking elsewhere I'd be suprised if this one cannot at least make the frame on debut.

Colt sired by Wootton Bassett and dam's sire Galileo, so six furlongs will be fine at this period of time, but further will be suitable. Massive price from Aiden O'Brien stable and could be mixing it with his stablemate Flushing Meadows, who is also a Wootton Bassett sired colt.

Made a solid debut in a similar level maiden over today's C/D, when keeping on well to come 7/21 beaten 9 lengths. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, good jockey retains ride and very shrewd trainer is 3rd best with his 2yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 33/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Jannah Star is a 3-year-old filly trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien. She made an encouraging debut and is sired by Sea The Stars, the winner of the 2000 Guineas, the Derby, and the Arc. She is a full sister to four individual winners who posted career-high RPR of 78-102-117-115. Beaten just 2 lengths when sent off 11-8f on debut behind horses with experience, she should come on for that run. She is my short-priced banker of the day under Dylan Browne McMonagle, who retains the ride.
Feel like the form of the debut race is solid, and I reckon Tenoya looks to be a good bet here for a yard that is well in form at the moment.

It is hard to look away from Wootton Bassett sired progenies, as this one is sired by him. Diamond Exchange from Mrs. John Harrington's stable looks to be progressing with sixth on debut and second last time out behind Butterfly Wings at Leopardstown. She could be achieving the win. She is 100/1 for the Irish Oaks. Connections think highly of her with a declaration of this status.
It's A Heartbeat belied her 50-1 odds when finishing 4th in her first race at Naas behind Kalixa and she may have been even closer but for being denied a clear run two furlongs out and losing ground.

Dam won over 1m6f and half brother Duke de Sessa was a 1m 4f Listed winner in Ireland before shipping off to Australia to win the Group 1 Caulfield Cup so this one should stay and might have some class. Has shown some ability in two maidens improving each time over trips likely to be too short and though has to improve the extra yardage coukd well bring that. Yard in fair form with four winners from last twenty sent out and with first time cheek pieces on I'm expecting a big run. Looks a cracking EW play and will be one for handicaps after this but must go well with step up in trip sure to suit on pedigree.

Ran in the same race as Tenoya, who was 3rd. Earthsong was 6th and last but started really slowly and was never in it from the start. I often think when that happens that jockeys don't really try, and for a 2-year-old on debut, they're probably right. Just give it the experience and try not to be too far behind at the finish. Thought highly enough of to be entered in the Irish Oaks, so let's see today if that is merited.

Went off fav in first attempt at 5f to be beaten by a head after not the smoothest run-in to the line. Off the same mark today, whereas Red Evolution is up 2lb. Has a handy draw and has the best chance here.

Solid 2yo who won a maiden on 3yo return and was unlucky in running in a decent listed event over 5f @ Naas Lto, when making good headway but denied a clear run 2f out, coming 4/7 beaten 4 lengths. Only 1lb higher in this handicap, good jockey retains ride and although top trainer is 0/31 last 14 days, her horses have been running with merit in that period, making current 16/1 very good Ew value in the race.

Trained by W.McCreery who has his runners in fine current form. Winner last time out at Tipperary. Led from early stages. Now runs in handicaps for first time and is clearly improving. Hasn't the best of draws but looks well in at the weights.

Was 2nd here on 2yo debut and returned this season with a win at Sligo. Most 2yo runs were useful, but it's the win LTO beating current second fav Shoney that looks the reason to be backing today. Tricky race, but if in the same mood with blinkers back on with same front-running tactics, might be hard to catch.

It's twenty-two runs since W M Lordan last visited the winner's enclosure, so he must be due a winner soon, with his last forty ride stats showing seven winners together with ten places. Gazelle D'or won here on seasonal debut off 2lb lower and was a beaten favorite when last seen.
Has won two of three starts this year, producing a career-best at Cork (5f, good) 15 days ago, just edging out Jorge Alvares. Could be in the mix again.

Bit of a wild 5f premier handicap, but a chance taken on Lethimfly who just looked a big price. He was a decent 3rd last time in and around race-fit horses, and he could take the required step forward for that return as he did from run 1-2 last season. Pieces of last season's form point to a well-handicapped horse off a 3lb lower mark. Drawn alongside the favorite here, they could push each other into a decent forward position, with the high draw being a plus. Whilst he’s on the same terms with that rival, having a run in his legs will hopefully knock out any freshness in him.

Won very comfortably last time out. Up 7lb for her trouble but that may not be enough to stop her going in again. Can dawdle a bit sometimes at the start but if she gets away she looks booked for a place at the very least.

Has about 4l to make up on Red Evolution and Jorge Alvares, on similar terms, so there has to be improvement. But there has been support for her. Hayes is retained, and she wears a hood for the first time and is less exposed than most. Decent each way bet.
Smoke them Out was a bold second at Naas at the end of last season. With two runs already he'll be fit and could still prove better than his rating if putting it all together.

This horse got it together after his first two starts and did well enough in a valuable c2 last time.
Should be capable of better still after a break since then and connections know how to win these valuable handicaps.

Triumphed at Tipperary in April. Finished 5 and a quarter lengths behind Red Evolution, coming in last of 8 in a handicap at Cork just 15 days ago. While some competitors seem more promising, considering past performance and an in-form jockey with a 7lb claim, placing an each-way bet on the distance winner appears to be a solid option at 20/1.

Stella Alpina all but turned over a 1-3 hot favourite last time, losing by a nose in a protracted battle which included a late bump on the way to the line. Drawn next to rival Cold Hearted on the stand side, she might have to battle again to get her first win.
More experienced than many in this race and seems to be fairly consistent with three places in the last four runs in races of similar class. So really has to be expected to continue to improve.
Marlborough Place looks like a decent bet here in the 5:50. It has shown enough promise in recent runs to suggest a race of this nature is within reach, and this could be the day.
A couple of these have posted decent efforts but with his jockey taking off a huge 10lb the well bred Colter Bay might be good enough to get involved in the finish on debut.

Massive price filly who has raced twice here and has not been involved where it counts. She has been slow out of the gates, which does not help her cause. John S O'Donoghue trains this Wootton Bassett-sired filly and has booked Ronan Whelan to ride. With the filly trained on the track with the stable here, she could be putting in some good work, with her not standing still in the stable after twelve days off.

SATURN SEVEN has won two races at 5f and 7f. Twelfth over 6f at Curragh on her latest outing last month. Course distance and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Last year's winner of this has to be the play in the bid for a repeat as has looked laid out for a repeat and off just a 3lb higher mark looks a cracking ew play. Was down the field on seasonal debut but the cheek pieces weren't on then and were reapplied last time to see an improved performance at Navan with a staying on third. Chris Hayes back onboard now too and with yard in decent form as stated earlier I'm expecting a huge run for this one from decent draw. As long as not too much rain about will run well.

I’m drawn to Richard Brabazon’s Gordon Bennett. The Curragh handler rarely races this 7 y/o outside of here and Naas. He’s got traveling issues. He’s a C/D winner, runs off 69 but has won off 90/80 & 73, so he’s a long way below his last winning mark. It’s easy to put a line through his last run; it was a 0-90. Prior to that, he was punted 12/1-4/1f and got carried wide entering the straight and was beaten by 5 lengths in a 0-70. The handicapper drops him 6 lbs since that, and given it’s another drop in grade today, his chance might not be far away. The booking of Dylan Brown McMonagle catches the eye also. Leading chance in a fiercely competitive handicap.

With White and Dynamic as non-runners today, Showhound stands a half-decent chance here. Showhound had been in good form earlier this year, including a tidy win at Newcastle. His latest run in a massive field didn’t quite pan out, but that was a tough ask. Blinkers go on now, and he’s likely to be sharper. If they help him focus, he’s got a decent each-way shout in this.

A midweek barnburner at the Curragh - what’s not to like about a 25-runner free-for-all? I love it. One that does catch the eye is Kevin Coleman’s fairly unexposed (on turf) four-year-old British filly KWA HERINI. She outran her odds on turf debut here at the Curragh over 6f (good) back in April. This daughter of BLUE POINT didn’t quite kick on in last month’s follow-up under similar conditions off a mark of 66, but she now drops 4lbs and gets what I’d call a pilot upgrade in the shape of Luke McAteer.
McAteer arrives here with a 43.48% place strike rate over the past fortnight (30.23% over the past month), and I always like my charges drawn high in these cavalry charges - stall #19 looks just fine. If KWA HERINI can reproduce anything close to her penultimate effort, arriving here 4lbs lighter, then completely ruling her out would be foolhardy.
Six Places on offer with more than enough to get involved. Lightly raced, a touch of upside, decent draw, and a jockey in form - it ticks a few boxes. I’m in.
In a big field and with 6 places up for grabs I am going to take a chance on Tawaazon who is a course and distance winner here at Curragh and won the race before last.

Verhoyen is a 10-year-old gelding trained by M C Grassick. M C Grassick is a winner of 8 races, with 6 coming at the Curragh, so clearly loves this place. He is a CD winner and handles today's good ground. Despite showing little or no form of late, he has consequently plummeted in the ratings and now sits 10lb below his last winning mark. At 18-1, he is well worth considering under Billy Lee and a trainer whose 15 wins at the Curragh is his biggest haul at any other track.

Secret Magician last won at Naas in August over 7f with rival Dynamic Force in 2nd. But his previous two wins were over 6f at the Curragh, where he often goes close. Drawn in stall 24, he should be involved in the finish.

Catherine Chroi with 6P on offer. She could be worth an EW as she was second at Naas back in March at 6f but could not keep up with the pace at 5f last time out. The return to 6f+ today is what makes her worth a chance at a great price.
Won on the last run of her season in October and would have needed her reappearance run last time after 7 months off. Comes here from an unchanged mark and is worth an each-way bet.

Another from my MTF notes, Run Forrest Run has been there since an eye-catching 25/1 third of seventeen in March 2023. Although the 7-y-o hasn't set the world alight in his twenty-three runs since, he has notched up three wins as well as three places. He ran a corker after missing the break to finish third on second start for trainer Thomas Coyle and if starting without a glitch this evening he has solid claims.

This horse showed promising form in maidens and should make up into a useful handicapper, especially now that he is stable and accompanied by an in-form jockey claiming 4 lbs. Could be anything and looks valuable to battle out the finish.
No comment made

This 1m6f Premier Handicap looks very hot with just under 30,000 euros prizemoney up for grabs. Some usual suspects and many dual purpose horses, including the selection, Joseph O'Brien (SR 15%) trained Mr Percy. Actually runs off bottom weight here with the lowest rating of all of 87. Wayne Hassett further claims a 5lbs allowance. Form record is a strong one. Eight runs since joining the yard have resulted in three wins, three second places and the two no shows can be put down to bad jumping errors. 16-1 winner of a Grade 2 novice hurdle when last out in April. Ran second, beaten a neck, in sole previous handicap run on the Flat at Galway at this trip (August last year). Has shown a lot of promise and could easily be well in on current handicap mark. By Derby winner Sir Percy. Nice sort.

A recent winner over hurdles in a conditions race at Cork over two miles. Progressive type who runs off a useful handicap mark on the Flat. Trained by A. Slattery. Has won off a higher official handicap rating. Consistent on the Flat with four wins, seven places from twenty runs. Strong each way claims.
Harbour Wind did not show up in the last race, and I think has unfairly been overlooked here. This horse has got decent form over the distance and I wouldn't be surprised by a good race here.

This canniest of all yards knows exactly how to tee one up for a long-distance handicap such as this. The selection was the victim of an awful ride from Kingscote in the 2024 Chester Cup, and hopefully, the engagement of C Keane is an intention of positivity. Plus, this animal can go well fresh after a well-deserved break.

Ex-Godolphin that is untried on decent ground but has been in and around the places on each of his 9 starts under rules. He bumped into a fair type last time, sent up in trip to 2m for the first time. If he can transfer that form to turf, on which he is admittedly 0/2, then he can be in the shake-up once again. His dam acted on this surface, so there should be hope that he can handle it, whilst also being related to a pair that did, and his AW form gives him a chance off this mark. With certainty, he will get this reduced trip. I’d hope he’s ridden a bit more aggressively than last time when he missed the break, and in a race that lacks pace, it could pay to go off the front end and set the fractions, though he could just be undone by classier rivals.

I think George Boughey's yard is going to hit a purple patch, and It's Tim comes over to Ireland today. I'm sure it's not for the scenery. It will have to improve again in this harder race than it's been winning in, but even with the LTO blip, it could still get a place.
Massive odds for a horse that has top speed figures and should do well in this field. Well treated on last year's form. Trainer is flying at the moment. Suited to the distance and going today.

Rion Rubette started her two-year-old career with two close 2nd places and was pushed into Listed and Group company, which she did not live up to. She has run in three handicaps this year, and her mark is tumbling, including a generous five pounds since her latest run, 8th of 20 in a 5f handicap. But she should be better suited to today's longer distance, and she is well drawn on the stands side.

STEEL MAGNOLIA has been placed in one race from four starts. Second over 5f at Tipperary on her latest outing in April. Upped in trip to 6f should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to go one better and win this race.

Showed plenty of promise in two runs at this track early last season and to a lesser extent in a pair of handicaps that closed out the season. His top RPR came first time out, so perhaps fresh will be a good time to catch him, and a 6 lb drop since last time out seems on the generous side.

Would have needed the run on reappearance last time and was running over the wrong trip. Back to a more suitable 6f today, drops 3lb in the weights, and has an excellent 3lb claimer taking a further 3lb off. Has a decent each-way chance.

This 3 year old is a lightly raced maiden who came 7th out of 14 in a maiden race at Ballinrobe 26 days ago. She is now significantly reducing her trip and is making her debut in handicap racing. She has shown signs of improvement with Denis Hogan and could surprise at 25/1, making an each-way bet a worthwhile consideration.
